title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 175 (Pawnee’s right as to extraordinary expenses incurred)

content.overview: Section 175 provides that the pawnee is entitled to receive from the pawnor extraordinary expenses incurred by him for the preservation of the goods pledged.
content.glance: Pawnee is entitled to receive from the pawnor extraordinary expenses incurred for the preservation of the goods pledged.
content.study: The pawnee is entitled to receive from the pawnor extraordinary expenses incurred by him for the preservation of the goods pledged. Current-law framing: right to recover (not merely retain for) extraordinary preservation expenses.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: The pawnee is entitled to receive from the pawnor extraordinary expenses incurred by him for the preservation of the goods pledged.

examples.title: Extraordinary preservation costs
examples.body: Pawnee incurs extraordinary expenses to preserve the pledged goods. He is entitled to receive them from the pawnor under Section 175.

hypotheticals.question: Pawnee incurs extraordinary expenses to preserve the goods. What is his right?
hypotheticals.analysis: He is entitled to receive them from the pawnor under Section 175.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: Pawnee may recover extraordinary preservation expenses from the pawnor.
essentialIngredients: Incurred for the preservation of the goods pledged
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 175 provides that the pawnee is entitled to receive from the pawnor extraordinary expenses incurred by him for the preservation of the goods pledged. This is a right to recover the amount, complementary to the retainer rights in Sections 173–174.
examples: Extraordinary costs of preservation are recoverable from the pawnor.
distinctions: Section 175 is a right to receive payment; Sections 173–174 concern retainer of the goods.
problemApplication: Conclude right to receive them from the pawnor.
keyTakeaways: Pawnee entitled to recover extraordinary preservation expenses from pawnor.
